Rolex Murder 2

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Another Rolex robbery leaves a British man dead and his American wife injured - but two suspects are in custody.

Unique Selling Point:
Exclusive video footage shows the terrifying moment a couple on holiday from Las Vegas were attacked and shot in Kyalami.
We track their journey together from the moment they were targeted by members of the Rolex gang, to their last words to each other.
An expert explains the structure of the syndicate, where and how they operate and who they sell the stolen goods to.


Summary:
Briton Mike Edwards (77) and his wife American Noreen Edwards (63)were on holiday from Las Vegas. They had lived in South Africa fro many years while Mike was Managing Director of EMI Music. A few years ago they decided to move to the USA permanently and had come back to say a final farewell to all their friends. On 5th January Carte Blanche broadcast the story of the Piet Hoffman Rolex murder and the subsequent botched police investigation. ON 7th January Mike Edwards was shot dead for his Role watch, despite his friends and his wife, Noreen, trying to warn him not to wear it.
The couple were targeted in Nicolway shopping centre by a "spotter" who followed them around, from shop to shop, for almost 4 hours. When they finally drove to their accommodation in Kyalami they were chased down Main Rd by 4 men in a white Audi. At the intersection of Maple Road, 3 armed men smashed the car windows, shot both Mike and Noreen and stole only their Rolex watches. Mike died at the scene, and Noreen had surgery several times on her injured hand and chest. The incident was only reported as a botched hi-jacking and although the Deputy Director-General of the Department of Tourism tried to visit Noreen in hospital, it was never reported that the victims were foreigners.
Apart from the theft of the watches, Mike's brand new hearing aids, valued at R75 000, were stolen from the body bag at the mortuary after the autopsy.
On Thursday 20th February two suspects were arrested for the murder and attempted murder after an informant came forward to the JMPD.

Further information:
Bad Boyz security has been tracking the Rolex gang for several years and has gathered a lot of evidence of their modus operandi. He believes this is an organised crime syndicate with anything between 60 - 90 members. They are also involved in Cash In Transit heists, Bank followed-homes and truck hi-jackings. There are 4 major groups operating in Gauteng, and are known to the police.
He also believes that the there are several different buyers that are also known to the police.

This story will pose the questions what does the Rolex gang look like, and who are they selling the stolen watches to?
We will also try and ascertain if Rolex, Switzerland is aware of the problem of Rolex robberies in Johannesburg.

Extra Budget Items:
Possibly an extra day's shoot, depending how far we get with our investigation into the "buyers" of watches.

Script:


ROLEX MURDER 2

V/O: On the 5th of January Carte Blanche broadcast a story about a 2018 murder in Sandton. Durban couple Piet and Nicole Hoffman had been followed into the basement parking of their Grayston Drive hotel. Three armed men jumped out of a Mercedes Benz and started shooting. Piet was shot dead and the killers fled the scene with his Rolex watch.

Derek: Two days after our last story about a Rolex murder, another tragedy happened. This time it was a couple from America.

V/O: Mike and Norine Edwards had moved back to Las Vegas after 30 years in South Africa. 77-year-old British citizen Mike had been the General Manager of EMI Music before retiring.

Norine: This trip we were coming just to say goodbye to the people in Joburg that we hadn’t said goodbye to.

V/O: Both Norine and Mike had Rolex watches, which their friends warned them not to wear in public.

Norine: So I took mine off, but my husband didn’t. And then we went to Sandton I had it off, and Mike said to me look around Norine, this is silly look - and he was right. Everybody had bling, bling, bling and watches and you know, I just said you right and I put my watch back on.

V/O: On the 7th of January the couple went to Nicolway shopping centre in Bryanston. They were there for 3 hours waiting to check into their accommodation in Kyalami. While they casually shopped and ate lunch, they were being followed by two men.

Derek: Did you notice anything strange or uncomfortable there?

Norine: No.

V/O: At 1 o’clock Norine drove out of Nicolway and headed toward Kyalami, unaware that a white Audi was on their tail. Eleven kilometres later, she stopped at the traffic lights at the intersection of Main and Maple Roads.

Norine: There was a white car in front and I stopped behind. All of a sudden there was a guy standing next to the car in front. And he looked nicely dressed and all of a sudden he pulled out like a gun but with a real long ending on it. I thought they shot through the window, but people say that no it was a hammer. I just remember the boom, boom, boom in my ears and, the glass everywhere. And then Mike saying drive, drive. I remember him saying "watch." He wanted the watch and.. so my watch is on this hand. And when I went to get the watch off, it fell to the back seat.

Ian: I would have been the first car at these lights, there was the suspect’s car behind me and the victim’s car behind that. I looked in the rear-view mirrors and saw what I thought was a smash and grab.

V/O: Eyewitness Ian was unarmed, so did a U-turn and filmed the incident on his dashcam. Two suspects are at Norine’s window which had already been smashed. As she starts reversing her assailant can be seen hanging out of the window, while his accomplice follows them in the white Audi. Her car careers down the hill, eventually hitting a ditch on the side of the road and coming to a stop.

Norine: Now I don't know if I'd already been shot by then or if that's when he shot Mike, but I remember having my hand up because he had the gun, thinking don't put your hand there you know because he will shoot through it and he did.

Derek: Mike had been trying to protect you?

Norine: Well I know he was pushing the guy, and that’s why I’m wondering if that’s why they shot him. I don’t know. I don’t know why they had to shoot us? Take the watches, take whatever!

Derek: And really they were after your watches?

Norine: Yes. They didn't take anything else.

V/O: Paramedics requested a helicopter to rush Mike to hospital, but he died at the scene.
Initially the incident was reported as a botched hijacking, not a Rolex murder. In February the police arrested two suspects in Tembisa, who were positively identified from Nicolway’s security camera footage.

Capt: The two suspects were taken to court on the 21st of February. But their case was not put on the roll. The prosecutor decided that no, as the police there’s more information that we need to get.

V/O: So, the case was withdrawn and the suspects were released, according to Gauteng police spokesperson, Captain Mavela Masondo.

Capt: But what happened on that day is that one of the suspects was wanted for another case. It was also a case of a shopping mall following. So, after he was released that day, so we arrested him but for another case.

Link: Over the years certain places have become hotspots for Rolex spotters. In reality spotters are anywhere that people with money are likely to be.




V/O: But the shopping centre mentioned most often by recent victims is Nicolway. On the same day that Mike Edwards was murdered, this man was followed home from Nicolway and held up by two armed suspects who demanded his Rolex. When he resisted he was shot in the arm. He accelerated into the estate, and has subsequently undergone two operations.
This couple was also followed home from Nicolway and held up for a watch that’s not a Rolex, but closely resembles one. The General Manager of the centre is Gavin Balsdon.

Derek: What are you going to do to beef up security to prevent spotters from targeting your patrons?

Gavin: We’re seriously looking at upgrading our technology side of CCTV cameras by having facial recognition, behavioural pattern pick-up points and just to monitor what’s actually going on with certain particular individuals.

Derek: Do you think you should be warning your customers that there have been these targeted attacks?

Gavin: It’s also very difficult to do that. We thought about in in the past, and it’s not Nicolway in particular. I mean people must be warned about wherever they go. It’s very difficult to identify and see who’s a spotter and who‘s not a spotter.

George: They watch everything, they watch your movements, they see what you’re wearing. They might even have been close to you to actually see what kind of watch you’re wearing.

V/O: George Moraitis is a security expert who advises his clients to put away their expensive jewellery.

George: Anywhere that you are showing off your watch or your jewellery you’re a target. You become a target.
V/O: Rolex Watch Company is upset about the reputational damage of these robberies. It is of extreme concern to us that the Rolex name has been specifically linked to groups of criminals in South Africa, often erroneously dubbed Rolex Gangs, who are routinely robbing individuals of their luxury items.
Link: Now we’ve been told there isn’t just one Rolex Gang, there are a number of syndicates with anything between 60 and 90 members. So what exactly are we dealing with?
George: Today we’ll arrest 5, tomorrow there’ll be another five, six gangs, the Rolex gangs. So how do you put a stop to that? It just grows, it multiplies, there’s no end to it.

Derek: And these gangs, do they just specialize in watches?

George: No. We have also found that some of them have also been linked to other crimes like cash-in-transits, house robberies, business robberies.

Link: Victims of Rolex robberies often think that they’re being hi-jacked, but it’s not the car that they want it’s actually your watch.

George: Easier to sell, quicker to get rid of, small, and the profits are better on the watch than what they are on the car.

Derek: Generally how much would these gangs make each?

George: Between 20 and 30 grand. A watch of a hundred thousand rand on the black market is normally half the price. But then everyone knows that it’s half the price and they’ll haggle them. They’ll say no, we won’t give you 50, we’ll give you 30.

V/O: But where are all the stolen Rolexes going? Who are these gangs selling the watches to?

George: Some of them have been ordered, they’ve been sold through to pawn shops, they move out of the country, on the web, you can find it anywhere.
V/O: Rolex advises owners to report watch thefts to the appropriate authorities. The model and serial number of every Rolex is recorded on an international database at the time of manufacture. For a watch to be flagged as stolen, they need these numbers as well as a full police report. Every Rolex watch comes in a box with an instruction booklet and guarantee. The serial number on the papers matches the serial number engraved on the watch, and guarantees its authenticity.
Peter: I’d say avoid buying new watches, newish watches or very recent watches without the papers.

V/O: Peter Machlup is a well-known used-watch dealer in Johannesburg. He advertises online, but sometimes buys and sells watches without papers.

Peter: Because the watch does not have its papers does not necessarily mean its stolen. There are lists that are available that we check on regularly as to stolen watches; there are updates. If we’re uncertain we can often call the watch companies to get updates.
V/O: The pre-owned luxury watch trade has recently boomed, and thousands of watches are traded online around the world. But many online watch dealers buy and sell watches without boxes or papers. They too rely on the manufacturer’s database to check if they’re being offered a stolen watch.
Solly: Once we actually get the watches we then take the serial number on the watch and we’ll phone Rolex ourselves, and we’ll say to them is this number 1 a real Rolex? Is it authentic? And Number 2 has it been black-listed or reported as stolen?
Roland: Oh well for us we check them against stolen lists.
Kate: And where do you find those lists?
Roland: Well Rolex for example sends us their lists, updated as it becomes updated with them.
V/O: But not all stolen watches appear on that list. We asked Rolex to check on Mike and Norine’s watches. While these have been flagged as stolen, Piet Hoffman’s watch hasn’t. That means the Rolex stolen from a murder victim, could have ended up on any of these sites.

Derek: George, a lot of dealers offer Rolexes without papers or boxes. Isn’t this dodgy?

George: I mean you’re not going to buy a car without papers, same thing with a Rolex watch or high-end watch. You’re going to offer some kind of proof or certificate. And if that watch comes off a person that’s been killed, he’s got lots of trouble coming his way at the end of the day.

Norine: Let people know and put pressure on the police to do more, to catch these people and make it not viable for them to do this.

George: Easier to sell, quicker to get rid of, small, and the profits are better on the watch than what they are on the car. Derek: Generally how much would these gangs make each? George: Between 20 and 30 grand. A watch of a hundred thousand rand on the black market is normally half the price. But then everyone knows that it’s half the price and they’ll haggle them. They’ll say no, we won’t give you 50, we’ll give you 30. V/O: But where are all the stolen Rolexes going? Who are these gangs selling the watches to? George: Some of them have been ordered, they’ve been sold through to pawn shops, they move out of the country, on the web, you can find it anywhere. V/O: Rolex advises owners to report watch thefts to the appropriate authorities. The model and serial number of every Rolex is recorded on an international database at the time of manufacture. For a watch to be flagged as stolen, they need these numbers as well as a full police report. Every Rolex watch comes in a box with an instruction booklet and guarantee. The serial number on the papers matches the serial number engraved on the watch, and guarantees its authenticity. Peter: I’d say avoid buying new watches, newish watches or very recent watches without the papers. V/O: Peter Machlup is a well-known used-watch dealer in Johannesburg. He advertises online, but sometimes buys and sells watches without papers. Peter: Because the watch does not have its papers does not necessarily mean its stolen. There are lists that are available that we check on regularly as to stolen watches; there are updates. If we’re uncertain we can often call the watch companies to get updates. V/O: The pre-owned luxury watch trade has recently boomed, and thousands of watches are traded online around the world. But many online watch dealers buy and sell watches without boxes or papers. They too rely on the manufacturer’s database to check if they’re being offered a stolen watch. Solly: Once we actually get the watches we then take the serial number on the watch and we’ll phone Rolex ourselves, and we’ll say to them is this number 1 a real Rolex? Is it authentic? And Number 2 has it been black-listed or reported as stolen? Roland: Oh well for us we check them against stolen lists. Kate: And where do you find those lists? Roland: Well Rolex for example sends us their lists, updated as it becomes updated with them. V/O: But not all stolen watches appear on that list. We asked Rolex to check on Mike and Norine’s watches. While these have been flagged as stolen, Piet Hoffman’s watch hasn’t. That means the Rolex stolen from a murder victim, could have ended up on any of these sites. Derek: George, a lot of dealers offer Rolexes without papers or boxes. Isn’t this dodgy? George: I mean you’re not going to buy a car without papers, same thing with a Rolex watch or high-end watch. You’re going to offer some kind of proof or certificate. And if that watch comes off a person that’s been killed, he’s got lots of trouble coming his way at the end of the day. Norine: Let people know and put pressure on the police to do more, to catch these people and make it not viable for them to do this. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Another Rolex robbery leaves a British man dead and his American wife injured - but two suspects are in custody.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Exclusive video footage shows the terrifying moment a couple on holiday from Las Vegas were attacked and shot in Kyalami. We track their journey together from the moment they were targeted by members of the Rolex gang, to their last words to each other. An expert explains the structure of the syndicate, where and how they operate and who they sell the stolen goods to.
metadata.Summary: Briton Mike Edwards (77) and his wife American Noreen Edwards (63)were on holiday from Las Vegas. They had lived in South Africa fro many years while Mike was Managing Director of EMI Music. A few years ago they decided to move to the USA permanently and had come back to say a final farewell to all their friends. On 5th January Carte Blanche broadcast the story of the Piet Hoffman Rolex murder and the subsequent botched police investigation. ON 7th January Mike Edwards was shot dead for his Role watch, despite his friends and his wife, Noreen, trying to warn him not to wear it. The couple were targeted in Nicolway shopping centre by a "spotter" who followed them around, from shop to shop, for almost 4 hours. When they finally drove to their accommodation in Kyalami they were chased down Main Rd by 4 men in a white Audi. At the intersection of Maple Road, 3 armed men smashed the car windows, shot both Mike and Noreen and stole only their Rolex watches. Mike died at the scene, and Noreen had surgery several times on her injured hand and chest. The incident was only reported as a botched hi-jacking and although the Deputy Director-General of the Department of Tourism tried to visit Noreen in hospital, it was never reported that the victims were foreigners. Apart from the theft of the watches, Mike's brand new hearing aids, valued at R75 000, were stolen from the body bag at the mortuary after the autopsy. On Thursday 20th February two suspects were arrested for the murder and attempted murder after an informant came forward to the JMPD.
metadata.Further information: Bad Boyz security has been tracking the Rolex gang for several years and has gathered a lot of evidence of their modus operandi. He believes this is an organised crime syndicate with anything between 60 - 90 members. They are also involved in Cash In Transit heists, Bank followed-homes and truck hi-jackings. There are 4 major groups operating in Gauteng, and are known to the police. He also believes that the there are several different buyers that are also known to the police. This story will pose the questions what does the Rolex gang look like, and who are they selling the stolen watches to? We will also try and ascertain if Rolex, Switzerland is aware of the problem of Rolex robberies in Johannesburg.
